newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Abducted Japanese in Philippines rescued-official. [corrected 13:10 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Abducted Japanese in Philippines rescued-official. [corrected 13:10 GMT]

text.p: A Japanese businessman kidnapped in the southern Philippines has been rescued and two of his abductors shot dead, the local governor told Reuters on Monday.

"They were all safe and unharmed," governor Priscilla Chiongbian said, referring to Kenichi Takayama (corrects businessman's name from Senichi to Kenichi) and several Filipinos who were abducted from a beach resort on Sunday.
Takayama and the others were rescued after police and soldiers shot and killed two of the kidnappers during a chase up a mountain in Sarangani island, said Chiongbian, the island's governor.

"The police are still chasing the rest of the kidnappers up to now," she said. Police said Takayama was abducted along with his Filipino companions while they were on a beach in the Glan town of Sarangani on Sunday. Another Filipino on the beach was killed by the kidnappers before they escaped with Takayama and their other hostages.

Kidnap-for-ransom has become a booming trade in a country Fortune Magazine has dubbed "Asia's kidnap capital." Police said the label was unfair, adding that while kidnapping incidents have continued, they remain under control.
